name: PwC and Strategy&
seo_title: PwC and Strategy& case study interview: what to expect
description: What PwC and Strategy&'s own careers pages say about applying, online tests and interviews, each line linked to its source.
intro: This guide sums up what PwC and Strategy&'s own careers pages say about applying and interviewing, from how to apply to how PwC suggests you prepare. It reflects those pages as we checked them on 16 October 2026. Processes differ by programme, role and country, so check PwC's careers site for your role before you apply.

items.text: For its Early Careers programmes, PwC UK lists the stages as applying online, an online assessment, a video interview, a virtual assessment centre, finding you the right role (graduate programmes only) and a business assessment, followed by an offer and then pre-employment screening and onboarding.
Strategy& UK says graduate applicants first submit a CV and personal statement online and complete an online assessment.
PwC UK says it will consider only one Early Careers application for its 2027 programmes, and anyone who is unsuccessful or withdraws must wait to apply for programmes starting in 2028.
Strategy& UK's FAQ says you cannot apply to PwC and to Strategy& at the same time, because you can apply for only one job within PwC UK in a six-month window.

On its graduate Strategy page, PwC UK says Strategy Consulting applicants can state a preference between Strategy& and Enterprise Strategy before the assessment centre, and that both roles are based in London.

PwC UK says the first stage for Early Careers applicants is a series of online activities and assessments, hosted on the SHL platform, that measure cognitive skills, behaviours, natural preferences and reasoning.
PwC UK says the cognitive test covers numerical, inductive and deductive reasoning and is timed, while the behavioural assessment is not timed.
PwC UK says candidates invited to the online assessment can take some practice tests before they start, and it points them to its Employability Hub to prepare.
PwC UK says the next stage is an on-demand video interview in which questions appear on screen and your recorded answers are reviewed later by an assessor rather than a live interviewer.
PwC UK's graduate Strategy page says the video interview questions focus on how you typically approach your work, for example at school, university or in earlier jobs.
PwC UK says the penultimate stage is a virtual immersive assessment centre, where it assesses you against the core skills and attributes it sees as crucial for success at PwC.
PwC UK says the final stage is an in-person interview with a senior leader from the business area you are matched to, held in the office you are matched to.
PwC UK's graduate Strategy page says that for Strategy Consulting applicants this final stage also includes a series of case study interviews with a senior Strategy& leader.
Strategy& UK says applicants who pass the online assessment and screening are invited to a first round of two back-to-back interviews, held either virtually or in person at its London office.

Strategy& UK says the first round typically includes an unstructured case study interview of about 45 minutes, which opens with questions about who you are and then gives you a consulting case to work through with your interviewer.

Strategy& UK says the first round also typically includes a structured case study interview of about 45 minutes, using a slide pack that reflects a real client project, with about 10 minutes to review it before you are asked to develop recommended solutions for the client.
Strategy& UK says its case studies are designed to show how you think when structuring an approach to a client's problem, rather than whether you reach the right answer.
Strategy& UK says those who pass the first round go on to a second round of interviews, either on the same day as part of an in-person full-day assessment or on another assessment day.

sections.heading: What PwC and Strategy& look for

items.text: PwC UK says it assesses early careers candidates against the PwC Professional framework, which has two dimensions: Trusted Leadership and Distinctive Outcomes.

For most of its graduate Strategy roles, PwC UK welcomes all degree disciplines and says what matters most is analytical thinking, curiosity and the ability to influence and communicate ideas clearly.
Strategy& UK says candidates are not at a disadvantage without a business background, but it looks for a strong academic record, intellectual curiosity and high motivation.

PwC UK says using AI tools, AI-enabled services or any third-party help to generate, edit, coach or otherwise complete Early Careers assessment responses is not allowed unless PwC explicitly authorises it.

In its interview preparation e-learn, PwC UK advises candidates facing case study questions to research the employer, its offerings and markets, and to understand key business concepts such as revenue, fixed and variable costs, profit and market share.
Strategy& UK says its insight events let you hear from its consultants on topics that include tips on preparing for the case study interviews.
For its Middle East offices, Strategy& advises case candidates to structure the problem, briefly explain the framework they plan to use so the interviewer can comment, and keep the framework simple.

practice_advice: Practise saying your structure out loud before you start any analysis, so the interviewer can follow your plan.
Do short, timed mental maths drills most days, with pen and paper only. Mock Partner's drills cover mental maths, chart reading and market sizing.
After each practice case, write down one thing to do better and choose your next case to work on it.
